mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPI) above 2% annualized over the past two months signals inflationary pressure, leading to tighter monetary policy expectations and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL annualized increase > 2% does not correlate with tighter monetary policy.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5 percentage points in the past month signals a weakening labor market, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 5d returns in > 70% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase > 0.5pp does not correlate with a weakening labor market.

mechanism_narrative: A significant drop in housing starts (HOUST) by more than 10% in the past two months signals a decline in demand for housing, which is a leading indicator of broader economic weakness, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or HOUST decrease > 10% does not correlate with broader economic weakness.

mechanism_narrative: An increase in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% in the past two months signals a strengthening supply side, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 1% does not correlate with a strengthening supply side.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is negative, it signals a combination of accommodative monetary policy and economic contraction, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of low FEDFUNDS and negative GDPC1 growth does not correlate with negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A steady increase in nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) by more than 200,000 jobs per month for two consecutive months signals a strengthening labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increase > 200k jobs for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: SPX produces negative 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or PAYEMS increase > 200k jobs does not correlate with a strengthening labor market.

mechanism_narrative: When real estate loans (RSAFS) decrease by more than 5% in the past month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) increases by more than 0.3 percentage points, it signals a weakening demand coupled with labor market stress, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 20d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or the combination of RSAFS decrease and UNRATE increase does not correlate with negative returns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) above 2% for three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: SPX produces positive 60d returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or FEDFUNDS > 2% for 3 months does not correlate with tightening monetary policy.
